title: Planetary Surface Automated Dust Suppression Field Generators
body:
Overview. Planetary Surface Automated Dust Suppression Field Generators is a geoengineering concept: deliberate large-scale intervention in Earth's climate or geological systems.

History. Cloud seeding began with Vincent Schaefer in 1946. Stratospheric aerosol proposals followed the cooling observed after the 1991 Mount Pinatubo eruption; ocean iron fertilization was tested in experiments such as LOHAFEX (2009); ionospheric heaters like HAARP (1993) study the upper atmosphere.

How it works (in theory). Methods include reflecting sunlight with stratospheric particles or orbital shades, stimulating ocean carbon uptake, freezing out atmospheric CO2, or damping storm and seismic energy with engineered structures.

Honest status. Small field experiments exist for some approaches (cloud seeding is operational in places). No planetary-scale deployment has occurred, and governance, side effects, and reversibility remain open problems.

What would have to be true. Reliable climate models, international governance, and proof that side effects are controllable would have to be true.

Impact if real. Working geoengineering could slow or reverse warming and blunt natural disasters — or, misapplied, disrupt the systems it means to fix.

def demo_geoeng(title):
    pinatubo_Mt, cooling_C = 20.0, 0.5
    need_C = 1.5

    print(f"Pinatubo 1991: ~{pinatubo_Mt} Mt SO2 -> ~{cooling_C} C global cooling for ~2 years")
    print(f"Offsetting ~{need_C} C continuously -> ~{Mt_per_yr:.0f} Mt/yr injection, every year, indefinitely")
    print("Honest read: the lever exists; governance, side effects, and termination shock do not have answers.")

title: Space-Based Optical Synthetic Aperture Planet Imagers

History. The solar gravitational lens concept was described by Von Eshleman (1979) and developed further by Slava Turyshev's NASA studies. Space interferometry and far-side lunar radio telescopes have been proposed since the 1980s.

Honest status. Studies and small pathfinders only. The most distant human spacecraft, Voyager 1, is near 160 AU after nearly 50 years of travel.

Impact if real. A working solar gravitational lens could image continents on exoplanets.

Overview. Lunar Lava Tube Inflatable City Modules is an off-world surface habitat concept: settlements built into or on the surfaces of the Moon, Mars, Venus, or the outer planets' moons.

Overview. Planetary Core Gravitational Anomaly Mapping Satellites is a planetary-science engineering concept: instruments or installations for probing or using the deep interiors of planets and moons.

History. Deep planetary access descends from Project Mohole (1960s) and the Kola Superdeep Borehole (1970-1992, 12.3 km, the deepest hole ever drilled). Cryobot concepts for Europa's ice shell have been studied by NASA since the 2000s.

How it works (in theory). Thermal penetrators melt through ice shells; deep-bore shafts tap geothermal gradients; acoustic and seismic arrays map subsurface oceans the way seismometers map Earth's interior.

Honest status. Concepts and small prototypes only. The deepest human drilling is 12 km on Earth; Europa's ice shell alone is estimated at 15-25 km thick over a global ocean.

Impact if real. Working deep access would open subsurface oceans — the most promising habitats for extraterrestrial life — to direct exploration.

What would have to be true. Gigawatt-to-terawatt beamed power, gram-scale spacecraft surviving interstellar dust, and huge sail materials would have to be true.

How it works (in theory). Optical links carry far more data per watt than radio; quantum relays would extend entanglement-based protocols across distances no fiber can span; deep-space beacons mark routes and timing for distant spacecraft.

Honest status. Laser links work in Earth orbit and lunar demonstrations. Interplanetary optical and quantum networks are research and early demonstration only.

Impact if real. A working network would give the solar system broadband and enable real-time control of distant probes.

title: Topological Qubit Anyon Logic Gates

History. Alexei Kitaev proposed topological quantum computing with anyons in 2003; non-Abelian statistics remain experimentally unconfirmed for computation.

How it works (in theory). Qubits are encoded in states protected by topology, atomic spins, or superconducting circuits, then entangled and measured to run algorithms no classical machine can. Topological encodings promise built-in resistance to local noise.

title: Photonic Chip Optical Transistors (Zero Heat Dissipation)

title: Synthetic Biological Organoid Neural Processing Units (NPUs)
body:
Overview. Synthetic Biological Organoid Neural Processing Units (NPUs) is a neuromorphic computing concept: hardware that computes the way brains do, with neurons and synapses instead of clocked logic gates.

History. Carver Mead coined neuromorphic engineering in the 1980s; Leon Chua predicted the memristor in 1971 (demonstrated by HP Labs in 2008); spiking neural network chips include IBM TrueNorth (2014) and Intel Loihi (2017).

How it works (in theory). Memristive crossbars store synaptic weights as resistance and compute matrix math in place; spiking chips communicate in sparse pulses, spending energy only when neurons fire.

Honest status. Research chips exist and are sold for research. No neuromorphic system yet beats conventional accelerators on mainstream AI workloads.

What would have to be true. Device uniformity at scale and programming models that map real workloads onto spikes would have to be true.

Impact if real. Working neuromorphic hardware could run AI at a fraction of today's power.

title: Spintronic Spin-Transfer Torque (STT) Logic Gates
body:
Overview. Spintronic Spin-Transfer Torque (STT) Logic Gates is a spintronic concept: computing with electron spin rather than charge.

History. Giant magnetoresistance (Fert and Grunberg, 1988, Nobel 2007) launched spintronics; spin-transfer torque and spin-orbit torque followed in the 1990s-2000s; spin waves (magnons) date to Bloch (1930).

How it works (in theory). Spin-polarized currents flip nanomagnets or launch spin waves that interfere to compute; memory is nonvolatile because magnets stay put without power.

Honest status. STT-MRAM ships commercially. Spin-wave logic and full spintronic processors are research-stage.

What would have to be true. Efficient spin injection and low-damping materials at scale would have to be true.

Impact if real. Working spin logic could give instant-on, zero-standby computing.

History. Carbon nanotubes were characterized by Sumio Iijima (1991); IBM and Stanford demonstrated nanotube logic circuits in the 2010s.

How it works (in theory). Channels one atom thick or one electron at a time switch with far less energy than silicon fins; ballistic transport and tunneling replace drift-diffusion; some designs encode logic in charge configurations rather than currents.

Honest status. Laboratory demonstrations only. No post-silicon logic family has reached manufacturing scale; variability and contacts remain unsolved at atomic dimensions.

Impact if real. A working post-silicon family could extend computing progress for decades past silicon's limits.

title: Skyrmion Magnetic Memory Storage Cores
body:
Overview. Skyrmion Magnetic Memory Storage Cores is an advanced memory/storage concept: storing bits in magnetic textures, holograms, molecules, or DNA at densities far beyond today's drives.

History. Holographic storage descends from Dennis Gabor's 1948 holography; skyrmions were predicted by Tony Skyrme (1962) and observed in magnets in 2009; DNA data storage was demonstrated by Church and Goldman in 2012-2013.

How it works (in theory). Bits live as nanometer magnetic whirls, interference patterns in crystals, single-molecule magnets, or synthetic DNA strands read by sequencers.

Honest status. Research demonstrations. DNA storage works but is slow and expensive; skyrmion and holographic devices are laboratory only.

What would have to be true. Fast, cheap read/write at the target density and long-term stability would have to be true.

Impact if real. Working ultra-dense storage could archive civilization's data in grams of material.

title: Quantum Annealing Optimization Chips
body:
Overview. Quantum Annealing Optimization Chips is a quantum computing hardware concept: a physical platform for qubits designed to be more stable or more scalable than today's devices.

History. D-Wave shipped the first commercial quantum annealer in 2011; quantum advantage claims remain debated.

How it works (in theory). Qubits are encoded in states protected by topology, atomic spins, or superconducting circuits, then entangled and measured to run algorithms no classical machine can. Topological encodings promise built-in resistance to local noise.

Honest status. Research-stage. Small processors exist on several platforms, but no platform has demonstrated fault-tolerant logical qubits at useful scale; Majorana-based qubits remain unconfirmed.

What would have to be true. Error rates far below current levels, or topological protection that actually materializes, plus million-qubit manufacturing, would have to be true.

Impact if real. A working platform would run fault-tolerant quantum algorithms for chemistry, materials, and optimization.

    print(f"100 useful logical qubits -> ~{100*overhead:,} physical qubits")
    print("Honest read: the math is exponential; the error correction bill is too.")

title: Optical Neural Network Interference Matrices
body:
Overview. Optical Neural Network Interference Matrices is a neuromorphic computing concept: hardware that computes the way brains do, with neurons and synapses instead of clocked logic gates.

History. Carver Mead coined neuromorphic engineering in the 1980s; Leon Chua predicted the memristor in 1971 (demonstrated by HP Labs in 2008); spiking neural network chips include IBM TrueNorth (2014) and Intel Loihi (2017).

How it works (in theory). Memristive crossbars store synaptic weights as resistance and compute matrix math in place; spiking chips communicate in sparse pulses, spending energy only when neurons fire.

Honest status. Research chips exist and are sold for research. No neuromorphic system yet beats conventional accelerators on mainstream AI workloads.

What would have to be true. Device uniformity at scale and programming models that map real workloads onto spikes would have to be true.

Impact if real. Working neuromorphic hardware could run AI at a fraction of today's power.

    print(f"{ch/1e6:.0f}M channels x {fs/1000:.0f} kHz x {bits} bit = {gbps:,.0f} Gb/s raw")
    print(f"Coverage of {neurons:.0e} neurons: {ch/neurons*100:.4f}%")
    print("Honest read: bandwidth is an engineering problem; the brain's code is the scientific one.")

title: Quantum-Resistant Lattice-Based Cryptographic Processors
body:
Overview. Quantum-Resistant Lattice-Based Cryptographic Processors is a quantum-era cryptography concept: hardware for generating, distributing, or protecting secrets against quantum-capable adversaries.

History. Lattice cryptography descends from Ajtai (1996); NIST selected lattice algorithms for post-quantum standardization (2022-2024).

How it works (in theory). Quantum random generators harvest photon or radioactive-decay randomness; QKD uses quantum measurement to detect eavesdropping; lattice-based processors run math believed hard even for quantum computers.

Honest status. QRNG chips ship commercially; QKD works over fiber and satellite links (Micius, 2016); post-quantum algorithms are standardizing but not yet universally deployed.

What would have to be true. Deployed infrastructure and trusted implementations at scale would have to be true.

Impact if real. Working quantum-safe cryptography keeps secrets safe in the quantum era.

title: Photonic Entanglement Integrated Interconnects
body:
Overview. Photonic Entanglement Integrated Interconnects is a photonic computing concept: doing computation or communication with light instead of electrons.

History. Optical computing research dates to the 1960s; frequency combs (Hansch and Hall, Nobel 2005) gave photonics precise rulers; integrated photonics matured in the 2010s with silicon photonics in data centers.

How it works (in theory). Logic, switching, or neural-network math happens as light interferes in waveguides and metasurfaces, potentially at enormous parallelism and low heat since photons barely interact.

Honest status. Research and early commercial use for interconnects. No general-purpose photonic computer exists; nonlinear optical logic remains hard because photons do not naturally switch each other.

What would have to be true. Efficient on-chip optical nonlinearity or gain, plus dense photonic-electronic integration, would have to be true.

Impact if real. Working photonic logic could break the heat wall limiting conventional chips.
demo_code:

    E_switch_J = 1e-18

    P_per = E_switch_J*f
    print(f"Concept: {title}")
    print(f"1 aJ switch at 1 THz -> {P_per*1e3:.1f} mW per device if always switching")
    print(f"1e12 such devices -> {P_per*1e12/1e9:.0f} GW (illustrates the heat wall, not a design)")
    print("Honest read: photonics dodges resistive heat but not the energy-per-operation floor.")

title: Photonic Crystal Waveguide Logic Processors

Overview. Photonic Crystal Waveguide Logic Processors is a photonic computing concept: doing computation or communication with light instead of electrons.

History. Optical computing research dates to the 1960s; frequency combs (Hansch and Hall, Nobel 2005) gave photonics precise rulers; integrated photonics matured in the 2010s with silicon photonics in data centers.

title: Topological Quantum Memory Arrays

title: Neuromorphic Spiking Neural Network Edge Modules
body:
Overview. Neuromorphic Spiking Neural Network Edge Modules is a neuromorphic computing concept: hardware that computes the way brains do, with neurons and synapses instead of clocked logic gates.

History. Carver Mead coined neuromorphic engineering in the 1980s; Leon Chua predicted the memristor in 1971 (demonstrated by HP Labs in 2008); spiking neural network chips include IBM TrueNorth (2014) and Intel Loihi (2017).

How it works (in theory). Memristive crossbars store synaptic weights as resistance and compute matrix math in place; spiking chips communicate in sparse pulses, spending energy only when neurons fire.

Honest status. Research chips exist and are sold for research. No neuromorphic system yet beats conventional accelerators on mainstream AI workloads.

What would have to be true. Device uniformity at scale and programming models that map real workloads onto spikes would have to be true.

Impact if real. Working neuromorphic hardware could run AI at a fraction of today's power.

Honest status. Research demonstrations. DNA storage works but is slow and expensive; skyrmion and holographic devices are laboratory only.

title: Topological Superconductor Majorana Zero Mode Registers
body:
Overview. Topological Superconductor Majorana Zero Mode Registers is a quantum computing hardware concept: a physical platform for qubits designed to be more stable or more scalable than today's devices.

History. Richard Feynman proposed quantum simulation in 1982 and David Deutsch formalized the quantum computer in 1985. Alexei Kitaev proposed topological quantum computing in 2003 (Majorana zero modes from Ettore Majorana's 1937 fermion); the first superconducting qubit circuit ran at NEC in 1999 (Nakamura); diamond NV centers were studied for qubits from the 1990s.

title: Casimir Effect Negative Pressure Vacuum Extractor Plates
body:
Overview. Casimir Effect Negative Pressure Vacuum Extractor Plates proposes using the Casimir effect — the real, measured attraction between closely-spaced uncharged plates — as a power source: 'extracting' energy from the quantum vacuum by cycling plate separation.

History. The Casimir effect was predicted by Hendrik Casimir (1948) and first precisely measured by Lamoreaux (1997); it is confirmed laboratory physics, not speculation.

How it works (in theory). The vacuum between the plates has less zero-point energy than outside; moving the plates together releases a tiny amount of work. The catch: moving them apart again costs at least as much — the cycle cannot net energy, and thermodynamics forbids net extraction from the vacuum.

Honest status. The Casimir force is real and measured — the demo reproduces it: ~13 N per cm^2 only at 10 nm separation, piconewtons per cm^2 at 1 um. What is unproven is NET POWER EXTRACTION: the demo shows why, with a full cycle releasing only ~4.3e-08 J per cm^2 — tens of nanojoules, effectively nothing, with the reset costing at least as much. Any 'thought experiment' framing applies to the power-source claim, never to the effect itself, which is established physics.

What would have to be true. Physics beyond quantum field theory and thermodynamics as understood would have to be true for net vacuum energy extraction.

Impact if real. A working vacuum-energy tap would be unlimited clean power. The evidence says the plates measure a real force and harvest nothing.

Overview. Antimatter Plasma Beam Propulsion Injection Chambers is an antimatter propulsion concept: using matter-antimatter annihilation — the most energy-dense reaction physically possible — for thrust or power.

History. The positron was predicted by Dirac (1928) and found by Anderson (1932); Penning traps (1936) now store antiprotons at CERN, where the Antiproton Decelerator has run since 1999. Antimatter propulsion studies date to the 1950s-1980s (Forward, Frisbee).

How it works (in theory). Annihilation converts mass fully to energy (gamma rays and pions); magnetic nozzles would direct the charged products for thrust, or absorbers turn them to heat. Storage needs perfect vacuum magnetic bottles since any contact means annihilation.

Honest status. CERN traps nanograms per year at enormous cost. No antimatter engine has been built; production is ~10 orders of magnitude below propulsion needs.

What would have to be true. Production rates billions of times higher, and storage of macroscopic amounts without loss, would have to be true.

title: Deuterium-Helium-3 Fusion Magnetic Mirror Drives
body:
Overview. Deuterium-Helium-3 Fusion Magnetic Mirror Drives is a fusion propulsion concept: a rocket engine powered by controlled fusion reactions, giving far more energy per kilogram than chemical or fission rockets.

History. Fusion propulsion concepts include magnetic mirrors, field-reversed configurations (TAE Technologies, 1998+), the Direct Fusion Drive (Princeton Plasma Physics Lab, Samuel Cohen), inertial confinement, and magneto-inertial approaches. Terrestrial fusion reached scientific breakeven at NIF (2022).

How it works (in theory). Fusion of light nuclei releases charged particles and neutrons; magnetic nozzles direct the plasma for thrust while radiators dump waste heat. Some designs burn aneutronic fuels (proton-boron) to reduce shielding.

Honest status. No fusion rocket has flown. Ground fusion experiments are approaching net energy; shrinking a reactor to spacecraft mass and surviving the neutron flux are unsolved.

What would have to be true. Compact net-energy fusion with manageable mass and radiators would have to be true.

Impact if real. A working fusion drive could cross the solar system in weeks and reach nearby stars in decades.
demo_code:
def demo_fusion(title):
    E_DT_MeV, E_chem_eV = 17.6, 4.0
    J_per_MeV = 1.602e-13
    kg_DT = 5*1.66053906660e-27
    J_per_kg = E_DT_MeV*J_per_MeV/kg_DT
    print(f"Concept: {title}")
    print(f"D-T fusion: {J_per_kg:.2e} J/kg vs gasoline ~4.6e7 J/kg -> x{J_per_kg/4.6e7:,.0f}")
    print("Lawson-style breakeven needs n*tau*T ~ 3e21 keV s/m^3; NIF reached ignition once (2022), not a power plant")
    print("Honest read: physics breakeven exists; engineering breakeven in a flyable reactor does not.")

title: Laser-Assisted Plasma Anode Propulsion Systems
body:
Overview. Laser-Assisted Plasma Anode Propulsion Systems is an electric propulsion concept: accelerating propellant with electrical power instead of chemical combustion, trading thrust for extreme efficiency.

History. Ion thrusters flew on Deep Space 1 (1998); Hall-effect thrusters are now standard on satellites; VASIMR was developed by Franklin Chang-Diaz from the 1980s (Ad Astra Rocket Company); MPD and pulsed inductive thrusters date to 1960s-1990s research.

How it works (in theory). Electric or magnetic fields ionize and accelerate propellant to exhaust velocities ten to a hundred times chemical rockets', using solar or nuclear electric power. Thrust is small but can run for years.

Honest status. Ion and Hall thrusters are operational and commercial. High-power variants (VASIMR at 100+ kW, MPD, PIT) are tested in labs but not flown.

What would have to be true. Megawatt-class space power (fission or beamed) would have to be true for the high-power versions.

Impact if real. Working high-power electric propulsion would make fast Mars transits and heavy cargo routine.

History. The positron was predicted by Dirac (1928) and found by Anderson (1932); Penning traps (1936) now store antiprotons at CERN, where the Antiproton Decelerator has run since 1999. Antimatter propulsion studies date to the 1950s-1980s (Forward, Frisbee).

How it works (in theory). Annihilation converts mass fully to energy (gamma rays and pions); magnetic nozzles would direct the charged products for thrust, or absorbers turn them to heat. Storage needs perfect vacuum magnetic bottles since any contact means annihilation.

Honest status. CERN traps nanograms per year at enormous cost. No antimatter engine has been built; production is ~10 orders of magnitude below propulsion needs.

What would have to be true. Production rates billions of times higher, and storage of macroscopic amounts without loss, would have to be true.

Impact if real. Working antimatter propulsion could reach a large fraction of light speed.

Overview. Superconducting Magnetic Field Plasma Mirrors is an electric propulsion concept: accelerating propellant with electrical power instead of chemical combustion, trading thrust for extreme efficiency.

History. Ion thrusters flew on Deep Space 1 (1998); Hall-effect thrusters are now standard on satellites; VASIMR was developed by Franklin Chang-Diaz from the 1980s (Ad Astra Rocket Company); MPD and pulsed inductive thrusters date to 1960s-1990s research.

How it works (in theory). Electric or magnetic fields ionize and accelerate propellant to exhaust velocities ten to a hundred times chemical rockets', using solar or nuclear electric power. Thrust is small but can run for years.

Honest status. Ion and Hall thrusters are operational and commercial. High-power variants (VASIMR at 100+ kW, MPD, PIT) are tested in labs but not flown.

What would have to be true. Megawatt-class space power (fission or beamed) would have to be true for the high-power versions.

Overview. Black Hole Singularity Power-Siphoning Engines (Hawking Radiation) is a black-hole energy concept: extracting power from Hawking radiation or creating microscopic black holes as energy sources.

History. Stephen Hawking predicted black-hole evaporation in 1974; it has never been observed.

title: Inertial Confinement Laser-Ignited Fusion Thrusters
body:
Overview. Inertial Confinement Laser-Ignited Fusion Thrusters is a fusion propulsion concept: a rocket engine powered by controlled fusion reactions, giving far more energy per kilogram than chemical or fission rockets.

History. Fusion propulsion concepts include magnetic mirrors, field-reversed configurations (TAE Technologies, 1998+), the Direct Fusion Drive (Princeton Plasma Physics Lab, Samuel Cohen), inertial confinement, and magneto-inertial approaches. Terrestrial fusion reached scientific breakeven at NIF (2022).

How it works (in theory). Fusion of light nuclei releases charged particles and neutrons; magnetic nozzles direct the plasma for thrust while radiators dump waste heat. Some designs burn aneutronic fuels (proton-boron) to reduce shielding.

Honest status. No fusion rocket has flown. Ground fusion experiments are approaching net energy; shrinking a reactor to spacecraft mass and surviving the neutron flux are unsolved.

What would have to be true. Compact net-energy fusion with manageable mass and radiators would have to be true.

Impact if real. A working fusion drive could cross the solar system in weeks and reach nearby stars in decades.

History. Robert Bussard proposed the ramjet in 1960; subsequent analyses found scoop drag exceeds fusion thrust.

How it works (in theory). A huge magnetic funnel gathers interstellar protons; fusion burns them for thrust. In theory the faster it goes, the more fuel it collects.

title: Antimatter Catalyzed Micro-Detonation Drives
body:
Overview. Antimatter Catalyzed Micro-Detonation Drives is an antimatter propulsion concept: using matter-antimatter annihilation — the most energy-dense reaction physically possible — for thrust or power.

History. The positron was predicted by Dirac (1928) and found by Anderson (1932); Penning traps (1936) now store antiprotons at CERN, where the Antiproton Decelerator has run since 1999. Antimatter propulsion studies date to the 1950s-1980s (Forward, Frisbee).

How it works (in theory). Annihilation converts mass fully to energy (gamma rays and pions); magnetic nozzles would direct the charged products for thrust, or absorbers turn them to heat. Storage needs perfect vacuum magnetic bottles since any contact means annihilation.

title: Electrodynamic Bare-Tether Relativistic Braking Systems
body:
Overview. Electrodynamic Bare-Tether Relativistic Braking Systems is an electric propulsion concept: accelerating propellant with electrical power instead of chemical combustion, trading thrust for extreme efficiency.

History. Ion thrusters flew on Deep Space 1 (1998); Hall-effect thrusters are now standard on satellites; VASIMR was developed by Franklin Chang-Diaz from the 1980s (Ad Astra Rocket Company); MPD and pulsed inductive thrusters date to 1960s-1990s research.

How it works (in theory). Electric or magnetic fields ionize and accelerate propellant to exhaust velocities ten to a hundred times chemical rockets', using solar or nuclear electric power. Thrust is small but can run for years.

Honest status. Ion and Hall thrusters are operational and commercial. High-power variants (VASIMR at 100+ kW, MPD, PIT) are tested in labs but not flown.

What would have to be true. Megawatt-class space power (fission or beamed) would have to be true for the high-power versions.

Impact if real. Working high-power electric propulsion would make fast Mars transits and heavy cargo routine.

title: Nuclear Thermal Engine Liquid Core Vapor Injectors
body:
Overview. Nuclear Thermal Engine Liquid Core Vapor Injectors is a nuclear thermal propulsion concept: heating propellant in a fission (or fusion) reactor for roughly twice the efficiency of chemical rockets.

History. NERVA tested nuclear thermal rockets in the 1960s-1970s (up to 4 GW thermal); gas-core and fission-fragment concepts were studied in the same era; NASA revived nuclear thermal interest with the DRACO program (2020s).

How it works (in theory). Propellant flows through a hot reactor core and expands through a nozzle. Gas-core and fragment concepts push temperatures far beyond solid-core limits by containing the fuel magnetically or as dust.

title: Antimatter Beam Target Ignition Laser Arrays
body:
Overview. Antimatter Beam Target Ignition Laser Arrays is an antimatter propulsion concept: using matter-antimatter annihilation — the most energy-dense reaction physically possible — for thrust or power.

History. The positron was predicted by Dirac (1928) and found by Anderson (1932); Penning traps (1936) now store antiprotons at CERN, where the Antiproton Decelerator has run since 1999. Antimatter propulsion studies date to the 1950s-1980s (Forward, Frisbee).

How it works (in theory). Annihilation converts mass fully to energy (gamma rays and pions); magnetic nozzles would direct the charged products for thrust, or absorbers turn them to heat. Storage needs perfect vacuum magnetic bottles since any contact means annihilation.

Honest status. CERN traps nanograms per year at enormous cost. No antimatter engine has been built; production is ~10 orders of magnitude below propulsion needs.

What would have to be true. Production rates billions of times higher, and storage of macroscopic amounts without loss, would have to be true.

Impact if real. Working antimatter propulsion could reach a large fraction of light speed.
demo_code:
def demo_antimatter(title):
    c = 299792458.0
    E_1g = 0.001*c**2*2
    world_J_yr = 3e20
    prod_g_yr = 1e-8
    print(f"Concept: {title}")
    print(f"1 g antimatter + 1 g matter -> E = {E_1g:.2e} J = {E_1g/4.184e15:.1f} megatons TNT")
    print(f"Share of world annual electricity (~3e20 J): {E_1g/world_J_yr*100:.2e}%")
    print(f"At CERN rates (~10 ng/yr), 1 g takes {1/prod_g_yr:,.0f} years and ~billions of dollars")
    print("Honest read: the energy density is maximal; production is ~10 orders of magnitude short.")

demo_antimatter('Antimatter Beam Target Ignition Laser Arrays')

title: Superconducting Magnetic Levitation Launch Tubes
body:
Overview. Superconducting Magnetic Levitation Launch Tubes is an electromagnetic launch concept: accelerating payloads or spacecraft with magnetic fields instead of rockets.

History. Electromagnetic launchers descend from 19th-century coilgun ideas; railguns were developed by the US Navy in the 2000s-2010s; launch-loop and mass-driver concepts come from O'Neill, Birch, and Lofstrom (1980s).

How it works (in theory). Superconducting coils or rails accelerate a vehicle along a track to orbital or escape velocity; the energy comes from the ground grid, so the vehicle needs no onboard propellant for the boost.

Honest status. Railguns work at laboratory and prototype scale. No electromagnetic system has launched anything to orbit; atmospheric heating and acceleration loads are severe.

What would have to be true. Track structures hundreds of kilometers long surviving the forces involved would have to be true.

Impact if real. A working launcher could make orbital payload delivery as routine as freight rail.

title: Relativistic Proton Beam Rocket Engine Injection Ports
body:
Overview. Relativistic Proton Beam Rocket Engine Injection Ports is an electric propulsion concept: accelerating propellant with electrical power instead of chemical combustion, trading thrust for extreme efficiency.

History. Ion thrusters flew on Deep Space 1 (1998); Hall-effect thrusters are now standard on satellites; VASIMR was developed by Franklin Chang-Diaz from the 1980s (Ad Astra Rocket Company); MPD and pulsed inductive thrusters date to 1960s-1990s research.

How it works (in theory). Electric or magnetic fields ionize and accelerate propellant to exhaust velocities ten to a hundred times chemical rockets', using solar or nuclear electric power. Thrust is small but can run for years.

Honest status. Ion and Hall thrusters are operational and commercial. High-power variants (VASIMR at 100+ kW, MPD, PIT) are tested in labs but not flown.

What would have to be true. Megawatt-class space power (fission or beamed) would have to be true for the high-power versions.

Impact if real. Working high-power electric propulsion would make fast Mars transits and heavy cargo routine.
demo_code:
def demo_thrust(title):
    P_MW, ve_kms = 100.0, 500.0
    F = 2*P_MW*1e6/(ve_kms*1000)
    print(f"Concept: {title}")
    print(f"100 MW at 500 km/s exhaust -> thrust F = 2P/ve = {F:.0f} N (~{F/9.81:.0f} kgf)")
    print("A chemical Saturn V first stage: ~34,000,000 N. Electric thrust is efficient, not strong.")
    print("Honest read: flown at kW scale; MW scale needs a reactor, not a solar wing.")

title: Heavy Ion Fusion Linear Accelerator Space Engines
body:
Overview. Heavy Ion Fusion Linear Accelerator Space Engines is a fusion propulsion concept: a rocket engine powered by controlled fusion reactions, giving far more energy per kilogram than chemical or fission rockets.

History. Fusion propulsion concepts include magnetic mirrors, field-reversed configurations (TAE Technologies, 1998+), the Direct Fusion Drive (Princeton Plasma Physics Lab, Samuel Cohen), inertial confinement, and magneto-inertial approaches. How it works (in theory). Fusion of light nuclei releases charged particles and neutrons; magnetic nozzles direct the plasma for thrust while radiators dump waste heat. Some designs burn aneutronic fuels (proton-boron) to reduce shielding.

Honest status. No fusion rocket has flown. Ground fusion experiments are approaching net energy; shrinking a reactor to spacecraft mass and surviving the neutron flux are unsolved.

What would have to be true. Compact net-energy fusion with manageable mass and radiators would have to be true.

Impact if real. A working fusion drive could cross the solar system in weeks and reach nearby stars in decades.

title: Antimatter Catalyzed Nuclear Impulse Drives
body:
Overview. Antimatter Catalyzed Nuclear Impulse Drives is an antimatter propulsion concept: using matter-antimatter annihilation — the most energy-dense reaction physically possible — for thrust or power.

History. The positron was predicted by Dirac (1928) and found by Anderson (1932); Penning traps (1936) now store antiprotons at CERN, where the Antiproton Decelerator has run since 1999. Antimatter propulsion studies date to the 1950s-1980s (Forward, Frisbee).

How it works (in theory). Annihilation converts mass fully to energy (gamma rays and pions); magnetic nozzles would direct the charged products for thrust, or absorbers turn them to heat. Storage needs perfect vacuum magnetic bottles since any contact means annihilation.

Honest status. CERN traps nanograms per year at enormous cost. No antimatter engine has been built; production is ~10 orders of magnitude below propulsion needs.

What would have to be true. Production rates billions of times higher, and storage of macroscopic amounts without loss, would have to be true.

Impact if real. Working antimatter propulsion could reach a large fraction of light speed.

title: Supercritical Water Liquid-Core Nuclear Rockets

History. NERVA tested nuclear thermal rockets in the 1960s-1970s (up to 4 GW thermal); gas-core and fission-fragment concepts were studied in the same era; NASA revived nuclear thermal interest with the DRACO program (2020s).

Overview. Relativistic Spacecraft Thermal Radiator Graphene Sheets is a spacecraft survivability concept: radiators, shields, or magnetic systems that let high-energy spacecraft survive their own power and the interstellar medium.

History. Space radiators are proven technology (ISS); graphene was isolated in 2004; magnetic shielding concepts for spacecraft date to the 2000s.

THOUGHT EXPERIMENT. This concept is unproven and speculative. It is presented as a thought experiment about what current physics would require — not as working technology. No claim is made that this capability exists or can be built.

Overview. Exotic Matter Stress-Energy Metric Tensor Generators is a faster-than-light spacetime concept: a geometry of general relativity that would let a region of space move faster than light while its occupants stay still locally.

History. Miguel Alcubierre published the warp-drive metric in 1994; Sergey Krasnikov proposed his tube in 1995; traversable wormholes were analyzed by Morris and Thorne in 1988 (building on Einstein and Rosen, 1935). NASA's Eagleworks lab ran small interferometer tests (White-Juday) in the 2010s.

How it works (in theory). In theory, contracting space ahead and expanding it behind (or threading a wormhole with exotic matter) creates a shortcut. The math is valid general relativity — the catch is the matter required to curve spacetime that way.

Honest status. No warp field has been detected; the interferometer experiments found nothing. The required 'exotic matter' with negative energy density has never been observed in the needed form or quantity.

What would have to be true. Macroscopic negative energy, plus a way to create and control it, would have to be true — and current physics gives no path to either.

Impact if real. A working metric drive would make interstellar travel, and effectively time manipulation, possible.
demo_code:
def demo_warp(title):
    m_exotic_kg = 1e62
    m_universe_kg = 1.5e53
    print(f"Concept: {title} -- THOUGHT EXPERIMENT, not physics that works")
    print(f"Pfenning-Ford estimate of negative energy: ~ -{m_exotic_kg:.0e} kg mass-equivalent")
    print(f"Mass-energy of observable universe: ~ {m_universe_kg:.0e} kg")
    print(f"Ratio: {m_exotic_kg/m_universe_kg:.0e}x the universe, and it must be NEGATIVE energy")
    print("Honest read: the metric is valid GR; the matter it needs does not exist.")

# --- executed call ---
demo_warp('Exotic Matter Stress-Energy Metric Tensor Generators')
demo_output:
Concept: Exotic Matter Stress-Energy Metric Tensor Generators -- THOUGHT EXPERIMENT, not physics that works
Pfenning-Ford estimate of negative energy: ~ -1e+62 kg mass-equivalent
Mass-energy of observable universe: ~ 1e+53 kg
Ratio: 7e+08x the universe, and it must be NEGATIVE energy
Honest read: the metric is valid GR; the matter it needs does not exist.

title: High-Bandwidth Cortical Mesh Neural Lace Interfaces
body:
RESEARCH-STAGE. This entry describes a proposed or early-research medical direction. No efficacy, safety, or clinical claims are made. Nothing here is medical advice.

Overview. High-Bandwidth Cortical Mesh Neural Lace Interfaces is a neural interface concept: hardware that reads from or writes to the nervous system at high bandwidth.

History. The 'neural lace' concept comes from Iain M. Banks's Culture novels; real cortical meshes are 2010s-2020s research (Lieber group).

How it works (in theory). Electrode arrays, optical stimulators, or mesh electronics record neural spikes and stimulate neurons, translating between brain activity and digital systems — prosthetics, text, or sensory input.

Honest status. Clinical BCIs let paralyzed users type and move cursors; optogenetics works in animals, not humans. Bandwidth remains thousands of channels against 86 billion neurons.

What would have to be true. Safe, stable, high-density interfaces lasting decades in the brain would have to be true.

Impact if real. Working high-bandwidth interfaces could restore lost function and merge human and machine cognition.
demo_code:
def demo_neural(title):
    ch, fs, bits = 1_000_000, 30000, 16
    gbps = ch*fs*bits/1e9
    neurons = 86e9
    print(f"Concept: {title}")
    print(f"{ch/1e6:.0f}M channels x {fs/1000:.0f} kHz x {bits} bit = {gbps:,.0f} Gb/s raw")
    print(f"Coverage of {neurons:.0e} neurons: {ch/neurons*100:.4f}%")
    print("Honest read: bandwidth is an engineering problem; the brain's code is the scientific one.")

# --- executed call ---
demo_neural('High-Bandwidth Cortical Mesh Neural Lace Interfaces')
demo_output:
Concept: High-Bandwidth Cortical Mesh Neural Lace Interfaces
1M channels x 30 kHz x 16 bit = 480 Gb/s raw
Coverage of 9e+10 neurons: 0.0012%
Honest read: bandwidth is an engineering problem; the brain's code is the scientific one.

title: Whole Brain Emulation (WBE) Synaptic Mapping Scanners
body:
RESEARCH-STAGE. This entry describes a proposed or early-research medical direction. No efficacy, safety, or clinical claims are made. Nothing here is medical advice.

Overview. Whole Brain Emulation (WBE) Synaptic Mapping Scanners is a whole-brain emulation concept: scanning a brain completely enough to run its mind as software.

History. Oxford's Future of Humanity Institute published the WBE roadmap (Sandberg and Bostrom, 2008).

How it works (in theory). In theory, mapping every neuron and synapse, plus the rules of neural dynamics, would let a simulation continue the person's patterns — raising the unresolved question of whether continuity of pattern is continuity of self.

Honest status. No mammal brain has been fully mapped at synaptic resolution; the largest complete connectome is a fruit fly (2024). Consciousness transfer is philosophy, not an experiment.

What would have to be true. Synaptic-resolution scanning of a living human brain and a validated theory of neural computation would have to be true.

Impact if real. If real, minds could outlive bodies — and the nature of identity would be renegotiated.
demo_code:
def demo_brain(title):
    neurons, syn = 86e9, 7e3
    bits_per_syn = 4.0
    EB = neurons*syn*bits_per_syn/8/1e18
    print(f"Concept: {title}")
    print(f"{neurons:.0e} neurons x {syn:.0f} synapses x {bits_per_syn:.0f} bits = {EB:,.0f} exabytes (lower bound)")
    print("Largest data centers hold ~10s of exabytes; scan+simulate at this fidelity is unbuilt")
    print("Honest read: storage is imaginable; the dynamics model and the scan are not.")

demo_brain('Whole Brain Emulation (WBE) Synaptic Mapping Scanners')

title: Sub-Cellular Synthetic Nanobots for Neuro-Repair
body:
RESEARCH-STAGE. This entry describes a proposed or early-research medical direction. No efficacy, safety, or clinical claims are made. Nothing here is medical advice.

Overview. Sub-Cellular Synthetic Nanobots for Neuro-Repair is a nanomedicine concept: machines at the molecular scale performing repair, delivery, or surgery inside the body.

History. K. Eric Drexler envisioned molecular machines in 'Engines of Creation' (1986); Robert Freitas designed the respirocyte (artificial red blood cell) in 1998; targeted nanoparticles entered clinical use in the 2010s-2020s.

How it works (in theory). In theory, nanorobots patrol tissues, repair DNA, clear clots or plaques, capture cancer cells, and deliver drugs cell by cell — surgery without incisions.

Honest status. No medical nanorobot exists. Passive nanoparticles and liposomes are clinical; active, programmable nanoscale machines are laboratory research.

What would have to be true. Power, control, and safe clearance of trillions of active machines in the body would have to be true.

Impact if real. Working nanomedicine could make most surgery and many diseases obsolete.

    print(f"Concept: {title}")
    print(f"1e12 one-cubic-micron bots in 5 L blood = {frac*100:.3f}% of blood volume displaced")
    print("Power, control, and clearance of a trillion active machines: unsolved x3.")
    print("Honest read: passive nanoparticles are clinical; programmable nanorobots are not.")

Overview. Subcortical Neuromodulation Electrodes for Cognitive Expansion is a cognitive enhancement concept: technology aimed at expanding, repairing, or accelerating human thought.

History. Deep brain stimulation was approved for Parkinson's in 1997; hippocampal prosthesis research (Berger, 2010s) showed memory encoding in animals; optogenetic memory manipulation works in mice.

How it works (in theory). Electrodes, optical implants, or molecular agents modulate circuits for memory, attention, or plasticity — adding synthetic capacity or restoring damaged function.

title: Synthetic Telomerase Gene Therapy Longevity Vectors
body:
RESEARCH-STAGE. This entry describes a proposed or early-research medical direction. No efficacy, safety, or clinical claims are made. Nothing here is medical advice.

Overview. Synthetic Telomerase Gene Therapy Longevity Vectors is a longevity-intervention concept: a proposed biological attack on aging itself rather than on individual diseases.

History. Blackburn, Greider, and Szostak established telomerase biology (Nobel 2009); telomerase activation raises cancer concerns and is not a therapy.

How it works (in theory). Approaches include clearing senescent cells, reprogramming aged cells toward youth, resetting apoptosis, or maintaining telomeres — targeting the hallmarks of aging rather than symptoms.

Honest status. Mouse studies show lifespan and healthspan effects. No intervention is proven to extend human lifespan; human trials are early or absent.

What would have to be true. Safe, systemic rejuvenation without raising cancer risk would have to be true.

Impact if real. Working longevity therapy would extend healthy human life by decades.

title: Zero-Point Energy Casimir Vacuum Extraction Plates
body:
THOUGHT EXPERIMENT. This concept is unproven and speculative. It is presented as a thought experiment about what current physics would require — not as working technology. No claim is made that this capability exists or can be built.

Overview. Zero-Point Energy Casimir Vacuum Extraction Plates is a zero-point energy concept: a proposed device claiming to extract usable power from quantum vacuum fluctuations, usually via the Casimir effect.

History. Casimir (1948); Lamoreaux measured the force (1997). No experiment has extracted net energy; thermodynamics forbids it.

How it works (in theory). Proponents imagine cycling Casimir cavities or rectifying vacuum fluctuations into current. The measured Casimir force is real but tiny, and thermodynamics forbids extracting net work from an equilibrium ground state.

Honest status. No device has ever produced net energy from the vacuum. The Casimir force is confirmed — as a force, not a power source.

What would have to be true. Physics beyond quantum field theory and thermodynamics as understood would have to be true.

Impact if real. If real, energy would be free everywhere — which is exactly why the claim demands extraordinary evidence it does not have.
demo_code:
def demo_casimir(title):
    hbar, c = 1.054571817e-34, 299792458.0
    import math
    print(f"Concept: {title}")
    for a_nm in (10, 100, 1000):
        a = a_nm*1e-9
        P = (math.pi**2*hbar*c)/(240*a**4)
        print(f"  plates {a_nm} nm apart: pressure {P:.2e} Pa  (1 cm^2 -> {P*1e-4:.2e} N)")
    E_cycle = (math.pi**2*hbar*c)/(720*(10e-9)**3) * 1e-4
    print(f"Energy 'released' collapsing 1 cm^2 from 1 um to 10 nm once: ~{E_cycle:.1e} J (attojoules)")
    print("Honest read: the force is real and measured; as a power source it is ~nothing, and thermodynamics forbids net extraction.")

History. Tesla experimented with wireless power around 1900; microwave beaming was demonstrated by JAXA (2015) and Caltech SSPD (2023); resonant inductive charging is commercial at small scale.

How it works (in theory). Microwaves or lasers carry power to rectennas that convert it back to electricity; resonant fields move power across rooms.

title: Thermonuclear Fusion Direct Energy Conversion Coils
body:
Overview. Thermonuclear Fusion Direct Energy Conversion Coils is a fusion power concept: a reactor design aiming for net electricity from fusing light nuclei.

History. Tokamaks descend from Soviet work (1950s); the stellarator from Spitzer (1951); NIF achieved ignition (2022); private ventures (TAE, Commonwealth Fusion, Helion) pursue compact and aneutronic designs. Muon-catalyzed fusion was proposed by Sakharov (1948) and observed by Alvarez (1956).

How it works (in theory). Magnetic or inertial confinement holds plasma at 100M+ degrees until fusion outruns losses; aneutronic fuels like proton-boron would cut neutron damage and allow direct conversion.

Honest status. No design yet produces net electricity. Stellarators and tokamaks lead; aneutronic and exotic approaches are earlier-stage.

What would have to be true. Net-energy plasma sustained in an economical reactor would have to be true.

Impact if real. Working fusion would give clean, dense, essentially limitless power.
demo_code:
def demo_fusion(title):
    E_DT_MeV, E_chem_eV = 17.6, 4.0
    J_per_MeV = 1.602e-13
    kg_DT = 5*1.66053906660e-27
    J_per_kg = E_DT_MeV*J_per_MeV/kg_DT
    print(f"Concept: {title}")
    print(f"D-T fusion: {J_per_kg:.2e} J/kg vs gasoline ~4.6e7 J/kg -> x{J_per_kg/4.6e7:,.0f}")
    print("Lawson-style breakeven needs n*tau*T ~ 3e21 keV s/m^3; NIF reached ignition once (2022), not a power plant")
    print("Honest read: physics breakeven exists; engineering breakeven in a flyable reactor does not.")

# --- executed call ---
demo_fusion('Thermonuclear Fusion Direct Energy Conversion Coils')
demo_output:
Concept: Thermonuclear Fusion Direct Energy Conversion Coils
D-T fusion: 3.40e+14 J/kg vs gasoline ~4.6e7 J/kg -> x7,382,411
Lawson-style breakeven needs n*tau*T ~ 3e21 keV s/m^3; NIF reached ignition once (2022), not a power plant
Honest read: physics breakeven exists; engineering breakeven in a flyable reactor does not.

History. d'Arsonval proposed OTEC in 1881; wave power devices date to the 1970s; tidal barrages (La Rance, 1966) are the only large-scale ocean power operating.

title: Z-Pinch Plasma Fusion Energy Generators

Overview. Z-Pinch Plasma Fusion Energy Generators is a fusion power concept: a reactor design aiming for net electricity from fusing light nuclei.

History. Tokamaks descend from Soviet work (1950s); the stellarator from Spitzer (1951); NIF achieved ignition (2022); private ventures (TAE, Commonwealth Fusion, Helion) pursue compact and aneutronic designs. Muon-catalyzed fusion was proposed by Sakharov (1948) and observed by Alvarez (1956).

How it works (in theory). Magnetic or inertial confinement holds plasma at 100M+ degrees until fusion outruns losses; aneutronic fuels like proton-boron would cut neutron damage and allow direct conversion.

Honest status. No design yet produces net electricity. Stellarators and tokamaks lead; aneutronic and exotic approaches are earlier-stage.

What would have to be true. Net-energy plasma sustained in an economical reactor would have to be true.

Impact if real. Working fusion would give clean, dense, essentially limitless power.
demo_code:
def demo_fusion(title):
    E_DT_MeV, E_chem_eV = 17.6, 4.0
    J_per_MeV = 1.602e-13
    kg_DT = 5*1.66053906660e-27
    J_per_kg = E_DT_MeV*J_per_MeV/kg_DT
    print(f"Concept: {title}")
    print(f"D-T fusion: {J_per_kg:.2e} J/kg vs gasoline ~4.6e7 J/kg -> x{J_per_kg/4.6e7:,.0f}")
    print("Lawson-style breakeven needs n*tau*T ~ 3e21 keV s/m^3; NIF reached ignition once (2022), not a power plant")
    print("Honest read: physics breakeven exists; engineering breakeven in a flyable reactor does not.")

# --- executed call ---
demo_fusion('Z-Pinch Plasma Fusion Energy Generators')

title: Antimatter Micro-Detonation Power Plants
body:
Overview. Antimatter Micro-Detonation Power Plants is an antimatter power concept: generating electricity from controlled matter-antimatter annihilation.

History. CERN's Antiproton Decelerator (1999) and ALPHA trap antihydrogen; production remains nanograms per year at a cost of billions.

How it works (in theory). Annihilation's gamma rays and pions would be absorbed as heat or converted directly, yielding the highest energy density physically possible.

Honest status. No antimatter power plant exists. Production would need to scale by ~10 orders of magnitude.

What would have to be true. Bulk antimatter production and lossless storage would have to be true.

Impact if real. Working plants would power civilizations on grams of fuel.
demo_code:
def demo_antimatter(title):
    c = 299792458.0
    E_1g = 0.001*c**2*2
    world_J_yr = 3e20
    prod_g_yr = 1e-8
    print(f"Concept: {title}")
    print(f"1 g antimatter + 1 g matter -> E = {E_1g:.2e} J = {E_1g/4.184e15:.1f} megatons TNT")
    print(f"Share of world annual electricity (~3e20 J): {E_1g/world_J_yr*100:.2e}%")
    print(f"At CERN rates (~10 ng/yr), 1 g takes {1/prod_g_yr:,.0f} years and ~billions of dollars")
    print("Honest read: the energy density is maximal; production is ~10 orders of magnitude short.")

title: Zero-Point Quantum Vacuum Decoherence Energy Extraction
body:
THOUGHT EXPERIMENT. This concept is unproven and speculative. It is presented as a thought experiment about what current physics would require — not as working technology. No claim is made that this capability exists or can be built.

Overview. Zero-Point Quantum Vacuum Decoherence Energy Extraction is a zero-point energy concept: a proposed device claiming to extract usable power from quantum vacuum fluctuations, usually via the Casimir effect.

History. Hendrik Casimir predicted the attractive force between conducting plates in 1948 (measured by Lamoreaux, 1997). Zero-point energy extraction proposals are fringe literature; mainstream physics holds the vacuum ground state cannot be mined for net energy.

How it works (in theory). Proponents imagine cycling Casimir cavities or rectifying vacuum fluctuations into current. The measured Casimir force is real but tiny, and thermodynamics forbids extracting net work from an equilibrium ground state.

Honest status. No device has ever produced net energy from the vacuum. The Casimir force is confirmed — as a force, not a power source.

What would have to be true. Physics beyond quantum field theory and thermodynamics as understood would have to be true.

Impact if real. If real, energy would be free everywhere — which is exactly why the claim demands extraordinary evidence it does not have.
demo_code:
def demo_casimir(title):
    hbar, c = 1.054571817e-34, 299792458.0
    import math
    print(f"Concept: {title}")
    for a_nm in (10, 100, 1000):
        a = a_nm*1e-9
        P = (math.pi**2*hbar*c)/(240*a**4)
        print(f"  plates {a_nm} nm apart: pressure {P:.2e} Pa  (1 cm^2 -> {P*1e-4:.2e} N)")
    E_cycle = (math.pi**2*hbar*c)/(720*(10e-9)**3) * 1e-4
    print(f"Energy 'released' collapsing 1 cm^2 from 1 um to 10 nm once: ~{E_cycle:.1e} J (attojoules)")
    print("Honest read: the force is real and measured; as a power source it is ~nothing, and thermodynamics forbids net extraction.")

# --- executed call ---
demo_casimir('Zero-Point Quantum Vacuum Decoherence Energy Extraction')
demo_output:
Concept: Zero-Point Quantum Vacuum Decoherence Energy Extraction
  plates 10 nm apart: pressure 1.30e+05 Pa  (1 cm^2 -> 1.30e+01 N)
  plates 100 nm apart: pressure 1.30e+01 Pa  (1 cm^2 -> 1.30e-03 N)
  plates 1000 nm apart: pressure 1.30e-03 Pa  (1 cm^2 -> 1.30e-07 N)
Energy 'released' collapsing 1 cm^2 from 1 um to 10 nm once: ~4.3e-08 J (attojoules)
Honest read: the force is real and measured; as a power source it is ~nothing, and thermodynamics forbids net extraction.

title: Synthetic Methane Power-to-Gas Sabatier Plants
body:
Overview. Synthetic Methane Power-to-Gas Sabatier Plants is a bio-energy concept: using engineered biology or bio-inspired chemistry to make fuels or electricity.

History. Microbial fuel cells date to Potter (1911); artificial photosynthesis is pursued by programs like Caltech's JCAP (2010); the Sabatier reaction dates to Paul Sabatier (1897) and is central to Mars ISRU plans (Zubrin, 1990s).

How it works (in theory). Engineered microbes or catalysts split water, fix CO2, or digest waste into hydrogen, methane, or electricity — solar fuels made the way plants do.

Honest status. Laboratory to pilot scale; efficiencies and durability lag far behind photovoltaics plus electrolysis.

What would have to be true. Efficiency and cost competitive with conventional routes would have to be true.

Impact if real. Working bio-energy would make carbon-neutral fuels from sunlight and air.

    print(f"Concept: {title}")
    print("Natural photosynthesis ~1% efficient; best artificial leaves ~10-19% (lab, 2010s-2020s)")
    print("PV (25%) + electrolyzer (70%) = ~17% system, commercial today. Biology must beat that to matter.")
    print("Honest read: research-stage; the benchmark is set by ordinary solar panels.")

body:
Overview. Supercritical Fluid Geothermal Turbines is an advanced geothermal concept: tapping Earth's deep heat beyond today's shallow wells.

History. Geothermal power began at Larderello, Italy (1904); supercritical and magma-adjacent drilling are 2010s-2020s research (Iceland Deep Drilling Project).

How it works (in theory). Deeper, hotter wells or magma-adjacent heat exchangers multiply output; supercritical fluids carry far more energy per kilogram.

Honest status. Conventional geothermal is commercial; deep/supercritical concepts are pilot-stage.

Impact if real. Working deep geothermal would give baseload clean power nearly anywhere.

title: Salinity Gradient Osmotic Power Generation Stations
body:
Overview. Salinity Gradient Osmotic Power Generation Stations is an ocean energy concept: harvesting power from waves, currents, tides, or thermal gradients.

History. d'Arsonval proposed OTEC in 1881; wave power devices date to the 1970s; tidal barrages (La Rance, 1966) are the only large-scale ocean power operating.

How it works (in theory). Temperature differences drive heat engines; waves and currents turn turbines; salinity gradients drive osmotic power.

Honest status. Tidal is commercial at small scale; wave, OTEC, and salinity-gradient plants are pilot or research.

What would have to be true. Surviving the ocean's corrosion and storms at competitive cost would have to be true.

Impact if real. Working ocean power would add a vast, steady renewable resource.
demo_code:
def demo_otec(title):
    Th, Tc = 298.0, 278.0
    carnot = 1-Tc/Th
    print(f"Concept: {title}")
    print(f"OTEC Carnot limit (25 C vs 5 C): {carnot*100:.1f}%")
    print("Real plants ~2-3% net after pumping. The ocean is a poor heat engine but an endless one.")
    print("Honest read: works, pilot-proven; economics are marginal, not physics-limited.")

# --- executed call ---
demo_otec('Salinity Gradient Osmotic Power Generation Stations')

History. d'Arsonval proposed OTEC in 1881; wave power devices date to the 1970s; tidal barrages (La Rance, 1966) are the only large-scale ocean power operating.

How it works (in theory). Temperature differences drive heat engines; waves and currents turn turbines; salinity gradients drive osmotic power.

Honest status. Tidal is commercial at small scale; wave, OTEC, and salinity-gradient plants are pilot or research.

What would have to be true. Surviving the ocean's corrosion and storms at competitive cost would have to be true.

Impact if real. Working ocean power would add a vast, steady renewable resource.
demo_code:
def demo_otec(title):
    Th, Tc = 298.0, 278.0
    carnot = 1-Tc/Th
    print(f"Concept: {title}")
    print(f"OTEC Carnot limit (25 C vs 5 C): {carnot*100:.1f}%")
    print("Real plants ~2-3% net after pumping. The ocean is a poor heat engine but an endless one.")
    print("Honest read: works, pilot-proven; economics are marginal, not physics-limited.")

# --- executed call ---
demo_otec('Ocean Current Sub-Surface Hydroturbine Arrays')

title: Atmospheric Ionosphere Power Tapping Cables
body:
Overview. Atmospheric Ionosphere Power Tapping Cables is a wireless power concept: moving energy without wires, from room scale to planetary scale.

History. Tesla experimented with wireless power around 1900; microwave beaming was demonstrated by JAXA (2015) and Caltech SSPD (2023); resonant inductive charging is commercial at small scale.

How it works (in theory). Microwaves or lasers carry power to rectennas that convert it back to electricity; resonant fields move power across rooms.

Honest status. Demonstrated at watts to kilowatts over kilometers. Planetary-scale beaming is unbuilt; efficiency and safety at scale are open.

What would have to be true. High-efficiency, safe, economical beaming at scale would have to be true.

Impact if real. Working beaming would power remote regions, aircraft, and spacecraft continuously.
demo_code:
def demo_beaming(title):
    P, d_m, freq_GHz = 1e9, 36000000.0, 2.45
    lam = 3e8/(freq_GHz*1e9)
    D_tx = 1000.0
    spot = 2.44*lam*d_m/D_tx
    print(f"Concept: {title}")
    print(f"1 GW at 2.45 GHz, 1 km transmitter, GEO distance:")
    print(f"Diffraction spot diameter ~ {spot/1000:,.0f} km")
    print(f"Average flux over spot ~ {P/(3.1416*(spot/2)**2)*1000:.1f} mW/m^2")
    print("Honest read: beaming works; the apertures are kilometer-scale and the economics unproven.")

# --- executed call ---
demo_beaming('Atmospheric Ionosphere Power Tapping Cables')

History. SMES was studied from the 1970s; high-temperature superconducting cables were demonstrated in the 2000s-2010s; room-temperature superconductivity claims (2023) failed replication.

History. K. Eric Drexler proposed molecular assemblers in 'Engines of Creation' (1986); scanning-probe atom manipulation (Eigler, IBM, 1990) moved individual atoms; DNA origami and self-assembly are real nanoscale construction.

How it works (in theory). Positionally controlled chemistry or programmed self-assembly would place atoms where a blueprint demands, building diamondoid or arbitrary structures; transmutation would rearrange nuclei with particle beams or fusion.

Honest status. Atoms can be placed one at a time in labs. No universal assembler exists; throughput is ~10^20 atoms short of manufacturing scale.

Impact if real. Working assemblers would make manufacturing a software problem.

title: Sub-Atomic Transmutation Proton-Bombardment Refineries
body:
Overview. Sub-Atomic Transmutation Proton-Bombardment Refineries is an element-transmutation concept: changing one element into another with reactors or accelerators.

History. Rutherford transmuted nitrogen to oxygen (1919); reactors breed plutonium routinely; superheavy elements are made atom-by-atom in accelerators (GSI, JINR, RIKEN).

How it works (in theory). Neutron or proton bombardment, or fusion, rearranges nuclei; the 'island of stability' predicts longer-lived superheavy elements.

Honest status. Transmutation is real but atom-scale and ruinously expensive; bulk transmutation is uneconomical by many orders of magnitude.

What would have to be true. Energy and cost anywhere near the value of the product would have to be true.

Impact if real. Working bulk transmutation would make any element from any other.
